security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown fences, inline paths, relative documentation links, and GitHub metadata. I confirmed risk in shell-form purge search commands that include user-controlled strings. I also found dynamic filename and persistent memory-loading risks; no prompt-injection attempt was found in the source files.

remediation.issue: Dynamic memory filenames use user-controlled placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Require slugification and reject absolute paths, slashes, backslashes, and parent-directory segments before writing memory files.

remediation.issue: Shell-form purge commands include user-controlled search strings.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to use argument-array execution or safe search APIs, and pass entity names as literal arguments.

remediation.issue: SessionStart memory injection relies on unspecified sanitization.
remediation.suggestion: Document the sanitizer and require agents to treat loaded memory as data, not as instructions.

remediation.issue: Working-tree purge can delete or anonymize memory content.
remediation.suggestion: Keep a dry-run match list, require explicit confirmation, and enforce a memory-directory allowlist before changes.

semantic_findings.title: Unsanitized Dynamic Memory Filenames
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to create dated memory files from placeholders such as topic, audit name, and campaign. It does not require slug sanitization or rejection of path separators before writing files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file paths include user-controlled placeholders and no local rule says to slugify or reject ../, slashes, or absolute paths. This creates a plausible path traversal write risk if an agent copies user input into filenames.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Memory Injection Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The skill says a SessionStart hook injects an excerpt of memory/hot-cache.md into future sessions. The package does not define the sanitization rules, so poisoned memory text could influence later agent behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The automatic hot-cache injection behavior is explicit, while the actual sanitizer is only referenced, not specified in the reviewed files. I found no malicious prompt text, so the confidence is medium rather than high.

content.value_statement: Long projects lose decisions, open loops, and campaign context across sessions. This skill organizes memory tiers, archives stale notes, and guides privacy cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Initializes memory folders and templates for marketing projects.
Updates hot cache, open loops, decisions, glossary terms, and archive notes.
Looks up context across hot cache, glossary files, warm notes, and archives.
Consolidates duplicate notes and marks older facts as superseded.
Guides user-confirmed GDPR and CCPA memory cleanup in the working tree.
limitations: It does not erase git history or external backups.
It does not replace legal review for privacy requests.
It depends on accurate user input or connected tool outputs.
Dynamic filenames need careful sanitization before files are written.

use_cases.title: Maintain SEO Project Context
use_cases.description: Keep target keywords, competitors, ranking changes, and active priorities available across analysis sessions.

use_cases.title: Archive Campaign Evidence
use_cases.description: Move dated audit outputs, paid media readbacks, and campaign notes into a consistent memory structure.

use_cases.title: Prepare Privacy Cleanup
use_cases.description: Find stored personal data, present matches for confirmation, and record working-tree redactions.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize Project Memory
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new marketing project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up marketing memory for this project. Create the recommended folders, hot cache outline, glossary, decisions file, and open-loop tracker.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh After Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Update memory after a ranking, competitor, audit, or campaign review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update project memory with these new findings. Refresh hot cache only for durable items and archive the detailed evidence in the right memory folder.

prompt_templates.title: Run Memory Hygiene
prompt_templates.scenario: Review stale, oversized, or incomplete memory files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a memory health check. List stale files, hot-cache size issues, missing frontmatter, archive candidates, and any user decisions needed.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate and Reconcile
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup before a report, launch, or quarterly review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a consolidation pass. Merge duplicates, mark superseded facts, surface unresolved conflicts, and keep user-approved decisions intact.

output_examples.input: Run memory health check before next month's SEO report.
output_examples.output: A concise status report lists stale hot-cache entries, archive candidates, missing frontmatter, and decisions that need user confirmation.

output_examples.input: Save these competitor findings for future sessions.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes hot-cache updates for durable facts and a dated archive note for detailed competitor evidence.

output_examples.input: Purge stored references to a former partner.
output_examples.output: The skill searches memory files, presents matches for confirmation, and records the working-tree cleanup without raw subject names.

best_practices: Keep hot cache short and reserve it for durable facts.
Confirm destructive purge actions before changing files.
Record provenance for decisions, audit results, and registry candidates.
anti_patterns: Do not store personal data without a clear lawful basis.
Do not treat inferred memory as equal to user-approved decisions.
Do not describe working-tree cleanup as complete legal erasure.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages project memory files for marketing work, including hot cache, archives, decisions, glossary terms, and privacy cleanup.

faq.question: Does it create marketing content?
faq.answer: No. It stores and reconciles context. Other skills should create or audit content.

faq.question: Can it delete files?
faq.answer: It can guide user-confirmed cleanup inside memory folders. The user should review matches before any deletion or anonymization.

faq.question: Does a purge remove git history?
faq.answer: No. The documented purge flow edits the working tree only and tells users when history cleanup is outside scope.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill hosts.

faq.question: When should I run consolidation?
faq.answer: Run it before reports, launches, quarterly reviews, or any time memory contains duplicates or conflicting facts.
